author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Store Gap
challenge.description: A batch of till scan lines from the northern stores was silently dropped during last night's ingestion, causing the model to forecast zero demand for fresh produce. #reliability_ruth# argues that the ingestion pipeline must be fully automated to guarantee every store's data arrives on time, while #data_dave# is willing to accept a manual verification step to ensure data quality before it reaches the feature store.

output.content: The hand over from versioning to the feature store is where I see the most risk. If the automated trigger keeps firing on bad batches, the feature store becomes unstable and the whole forecast job fails. I am prepared to accept a manual trigger for this specific step. It means a human has to confirm the batch is clean before it lands. I would give up the speed of full automation here. The trade is worth it because a stable feature store matters more to me than saving ten minutes of manual checking every night. I can live with that delay if it keeps the downstream data trustworthy.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are prepared to give up the speed of full automation in exchange for the stability of the feature store.
